brief: Banks that financed the AI infrastructure boom are retreating from that exposure, tied by the FT to Jensen Huang's exit from Nvidia and to regulatory fears after the Democrats' midterm sweep. ING and Société Générale have listed up to $800 million of data center loans for sale, including debt tied to Oracle's Stargate projects; the power-delayed Jupiter site is pricing near stressed levels while the Lighthouse and Frontier loans price higher, described as routine trimming rather than distress. Because confidentiality clauses on many of these loans block CDS hedging, selling is banks' main exit, so larger deals, a $63 billion Anthropic debt package and $40 billion for SpaceX chip purchases, are being pushed into the 144A market toward insurers, pensions and private credit funds instead. The ECB's Financial Stability Review calls this shift a dotcom/subprime-style systemic risk, and the ECB and Bank of England are both now formally reviewing banks' data center exposure. Goldman's 2027 credit outlook treats this as a genuine oversupply problem: it forecasts nearly $1 trillion of new AI debt issuance in 2027, says AI credit spreads have already widened well beyond non-AI spreads, and stays underweight AI-exposed technology credit while favoring banks, health care and energy.
